posts.title: What if you could bring your agent into the browser?
posts.description: An experiment: a Chrome side panel that lets the coding agent already on your computer - Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity CLI - co-browse with you, using the page's WebMCP tools first.

posts.title: When a WebMCP tool returns an MCP App
posts.description: WebMCP lets a website hand tools to the agent. MCP Apps lets a server hand UI to the human. We built an experiment where one hands off to the other.

posts.title: Trying Jev with WebMCP
posts.description: Jev makes structured decisions instead of generating text. I built a small Chrome extension to see how far that model can go when calling WebMCP tools.
